in_arabic.name: عسب
in_arabic.long_meaning: عسب هو اسم عربي يعني النجم أو الشخص المهم، وهو مصدر من الجذر العربي ع س ب، ويُستخدم في التراث الإسلامي لوصف الأشخاص المهمين أو الأحداث الكبرى، ولعل أشهر استخدام له هو في القرآن الكريم في سورة النجم

in_urdu.name: عسب
in_urdu.long_meaning: عسب ایک عربی نام ہے جو تارہ یا اہم شخص کو معنی دیتا ہے، یہ عربی جڑ ع س ب سے ماخوذ ہے، اور اسے اسلامی روایت میں اہم افراد یا واقعات کی وضاحت کے لیے استعمال کیا جاتا ہے، اور شاید اس کا سب سے مشہور استعمال قرآن مجید میں سورہ النجم میں ہے

historical_references.reference: Assab ibn Umaiya al-Majashi was a prominent Arab poet during the Umayyad Caliphate in the early 8th century. He was known for his panegyric poetry, which praised the caliphs and their military campaigns. Assab's most famous work is a lengthy poem dedicated to Caliph Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik, in which he celebrates his military conquests in Spain and North Africa.
historical_references.context: Umayyad Caliphate, panegyric poetry, military conquests in Spain and North Africa

historical_references.reference: Assab al-Nabati was a 9th-century Andalusian scholar and physician who wrote extensively on botanical and agricultural topics. He is best known for his work Al-Farq bayn al-Adwiya al-Mufradah wa'l-Ajwaj wa'l-Adwiya al-Tibia (The Differences Between Simple Drugs and Poisons and Medicinal Drugs). In this work, Assab compiled a comprehensive list of plants and their medicinal uses, making it an important source for early Arabic botanical knowledge.
historical_references.context: Andalusian scholar, botanical and agricultural knowledge, medicinal uses of plants
